NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) Q3 2025 Earnings Call Transcript November 20, 2024.

Executives Present:
Jensen Huang - President and Chief Executive Officer
Colette Kress - Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer
Stewart Stecker - Vice President of Investor Relations

Analysts Present:
Toshiya Hari - Goldman Sachs
Atif Malik - Citi
Vivek Arya - Bank of America Securities
Joe Moore - Morgan Stanley
Timothy Arcuri - UBS

[SECTION: PREPARED_REMARKS]
Operator: Good afternoon. My name is Kevin, and I will be your conference operator today. At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to NVIDIA's Third Quarter Fiscal 2025 Earnings Conference Call. All lines have been placed on mute to prevent any background noise. After the speakers' remarks, there will be a question-and-answer session.

Stewart Stecker: Thank you, Kevin. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NVIDIA's conference call for the third quarter of fiscal 2025. With me today are Jensen Huang, NVIDIA's President and Chief Executive Officer; and Colette Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Colette Kress: Thank you, Stewart. Q3 was another exceptional record quarter. Total revenue was $35.08 billion, up 17% sequentially and up 94% year-on-year, well above our outlook of $32.5 billion. Data Center revenue reached $30.8 billion, up 17% sequentially and up 112% year-on-year, driven by demand for Hopper H100 and H200 computing platforms across cloud providers, sovereign AI nations, and enterprise hyperscalers.

Cloud service providers represented approximately 50% of our Data Center revenue. Networking revenue was $3.12 billion, down 16% sequentially due to the timing of optical transceiver supply, but up 20% year-on-year. Spectrum-X Ethernet for AI is gaining tremendous momentum, with tier-1 CSPs adopting our 800 Gbps networking switches.

Gaming revenue was $3.28 billion, up 14% sequentially and up 15% year-on-year. Professional Visualization revenue was $486 million, up 7% sequentially and up 17% year-on-year. Automotive revenue was $449 million, up 30% sequentially and up 72% year-on-year, driven by autonomous driving compute modules.

Gross margin for the quarter was 74.6% GAAP and 75.1% non-GAAP. GAAP operating expenses were $4.29 billion, and non-GAAP operating expenses were $3.05 billion. Free cash flow was $16.8 billion. In the first nine months of the fiscal year, we returned $26.2 billion to shareholders through repurchases and dividends.

Update on Blackwell: Blackwell is now in full-scale production. We shipped 13,000 GPU samples to customers in the third quarter, including engineering racks to OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, we expect to ship several billion dollars of Blackwell systems. Blackwell demand is staggering, exceeding our supply for several quarters into fiscal 2026. Hopper demand remains very strong and continues to grow into the fourth quarter.

Outlook for Q4 fiscal 2025: Revenue is expected to be $37.5 billion, plus or minus 2%. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be 73.0% and 73.5%, respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points. The temporary gross margin reduction in Q4 reflects the initial ramp cost of Blackwell architecture systems, complex NVLink liquid-cooled racks, and early manufacturing yields. Full year gross margins are expected to be in the mid-70% range, rebounding in fiscal 2026 as Blackwell yields mature.

Jensen Huang: Thanks, Colette. The age of AI is in full steam, propelling a global shift to NVIDIA accelerated computing. Blackwell is in full production, delivering up to 30x faster inference performance compared to Hopper for trillion-parameter frontier foundation models.

[SECTION: ANALYST_QA]
Operator: Your first question comes from the line of Vivek Arya with Bank of America Securities.
Vivek Arya: Thanks for taking the question. Colette, following up on gross margins: you guided Q4 gross margin to 73.5% non-GAAP, down about 160 basis points sequentially due to Blackwell ramp. Can you quantify the trajectory throughout fiscal 2026? Does Q1 mark the bottom of the gross margin curve, or will dilution extend into Q2?

Colette Kress: Vivek, happy to unpack this. As we discussed last quarter, Blackwell introduces groundbreaking new packaging, including CoWoS-L, extreme interconnect density, and full system liquid cooling. In Q4, as we transition from initial sample units to commercial production, we incur initial manufacturing scrap and ramp costs. We anticipate gross margins will hover around 73% in Q4 and into the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Once Blackwell reaches high-volume production maturity in Q2 and Q3 of fiscal 2026, we anticipate gross margins will bounce back into the mid-70s, normalizing around 75%. Overall, customer willingness to pay for Blackwell's unmatched total cost of ownership (TCO) remains remarkably high.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Timothy Arcuri with UBS.
Timothy Arcuri: Thanks a lot. Jensen, there have been supply chain reports regarding overheating issues in dense NVLink liquid-cooled Blackwell GB200 NVL72 server racks. Could you directly address these cooling and thermal rumors? Are thermal issues impacting your Q4 shipping milestones or delivery schedules?

Jensen Huang: Tim, thank you for bringing this up directly. Let me be 100% unequivocal: Blackwell production and delivery schedules are on track. There is no delay. When you engineer a 120-kilowatt, liquid-cooled, 72-GPU computing rack with thousands of cold plates, high-pressure quick disconnects, and copper backplanes, precision plumbing engineering is essential. We have designed and qualified multiple cold-plate and manifold cooling solutions with our ODM partners like Foxconn, Quanta, and Wistron. Engineering systems at this scale is an iterative collaborative process, but every single Blackwell customer delivery milestone for Q4 and Q1 is moving forward as planned.
